articles.title: Architecture as a Measured Intervention: Inside the Work of Atelier Guo
articles.summary: An architectural intervention is not simply a question of how much or how little to introduce, but of understanding precisely where and how to act. This precision begins with a careful reading of the existing context , including the recognition of the spatial, material, and environmental conditions that shape a place. It extends into the process of design and construction, where complex considerations are distilled into deliberate, coherent decisions. articles.title: Wujiaba Flight Path 1922 Park Pavilions / Potential Architects
articles.summary: Wujiaba carries a century of Kunming's aviation memory. In 1922, Tang Jiyao established Yunnan's aviation force here and built what is widely regarded as China's second airport; it was also from here that Kunming residents first looked up to watch airplanes take off. During World War II, the airport served as a base for the Flying Tigers and a terminus of the Hump Route.

articles.title: How to Plan and Visualize For a City That Has Yet to Be Built
articles.summary: While most cities develop gradually, building one from scratch is hardly a new concept. Starting with a blank site, however, brings its own set of challenges. Rather than responding to an existing urban fabric, planners must anticipate how an entire environment will function, from its streets and infrastructure to its public spaces and the relationships between them.

articles.title: Why Does the Same Floor Plan Get Drawn So Many Times?
articles.summary: A floor plan arrives as a PDF. It shows the existing layout of a small store slated for renovation, and the client has sent it over the day before the first meeting. Before anyone can begin sketching a proposal, someone has to redraw the plan, line by line, in CAD. Once the ideas begin to take shape, the same space is modeled again in another program, this time in 3D, to produce images and renderings. The furniture list goes into a spreadsheet, the presentation comes together in a third program, and the client's comments arrive by email, text, and voice message, often with screenshots marked u

articles.title: Palace of the Parliament in Bucharest: The Contested Authorship of the World's Heaviest Building
articles.summary: In the center of Bucharest , about a kilometer and a half from the Old Town, stands the world's heaviest building . The Palace of Parliament , the seat of Romania's legislature, occupies Dealul Arsenalului, a hill at the western end of Bulevardul Unirii. This straight avenue crosses the city centre from east to west for roughly three kilometers, passing through Piața Unirii, before ending in front of the palace's main façade, which rises 84 metres in stepped tiers of stone.

articles.title: House Y / monotrum
articles.summary: A renovation project that transforms the client's childhood home into a residence for a couple and their two cats. The original house was designed to accommodate a family of four within a limited floor area. As a result, the priority had been to secure as many rooms and as much floor space as possible, rather than to create a comfortable living environment.

articles.title: Hill House / Taylor Knights
articles.summary: Hill House is a grounded, monolithic family home set atop one of Melbourne's prominent suburban ridgelines, overlooking Jells Park and extending toward the Dandenong Ranges. Conceived as a long-term, multigenerational residence, the project was driven by the client's desire for a home that could support personal life, professional activity, and evolving family needs within a single, cohesive architectural framework.

articles.title: Curtains Made Out of Aluminum or Wood
articles.summary: Nolastar , by German-Spanish industrial designer Pablo Octavio , is a curtain system made of aluminum or wooden tiles rather than fabric. Despite being heavier than fabric, the curtains are reportedly compatible with standard curtain tracks, whether motorized or manual. The Nolastar room divider and curtain system is more than just a functional element, it is a statement of timeless design and innovative materiality. It is a flexible system that structures, divides, and accentuates spaces without dominating them. It unites lightness and stability, transparency and privacy, function and design.
